metas.name: 1. Stark Raving Dad
metas.description: A deviation from his norm lands Homer in a mental institution, where he shares a room with a man who thinks he's Michael Jackson.

metas.name: 2. Mr. Lisa Goes to Washington
metas.description: Lisa's essay wins the Simpsons a trip to Washington, D.C., where her faith in democracy is shaken by her unethical Congressman.

metas.name: 3. When Flanders Failed
metas.description: Flanders suffers a failure after Homer wishes him ill.

metas.name: 4. Bart the Murderer
metas.description: While working for Fat Tony, Bart gains enough influence with his boss to solve his problems with Principal Skinner--perhaps permanently.

metas.name: 5. Homer Defined
metas.description: Homer's averting of a nuclear meltdown earns him employee-of-the-month honors--and a call from Magic Johnson; Milhouse's parents prohibit him from playing with Bart.

metas.name: 6. Like Father, Like Clown
metas.description: Bart and Lisa use theological arguments to try to reunite Krusty the Clown and his rabbi father, who disowned Krusty when he turned from rabbi to clown.

metas.name: 7. Treehouse of Horror II
metas.description: Maggie uses one of three wishes; a mind-reading Bart rules Springfield; Homer donates his brain to Mr. Burns' science project.

metas.name: 8. Lisa's Pony
metas.description: After disappointing Lisa, Homer buys her a pony, solving one problem, but creating others, requiring a second job--at Apu's Kwik-E-Mart.

metas.name: 9. Saturdays of Thunder
metas.description: When Homer helps Bart build a soapbox racer, it does little for the car but a lot for their relationship.

metas.name: 10. Flaming Moe's
metas.description: Moe steals the drink recipe Homer invented, and the rechristened “Flaming Moe” turns his tavern into a hotspot. When a national franchise wants to buy the recipe, Homer wants revenge.

metas.name: 11. Burns Verkaufen der Kraftwerk
metas.description: Burns sells the power plant to a German corporation that doesn't care for Homer's approach to his work.

metas.name: 12. I Married Marge
metas.description: A trip down memory lane to the early days of Simpson wedded bliss, when Marge was with child and Homer was without a job.

metas.name: 13. Radio Bart
metas.description: Bart fools the town into thinking there's a little boy trapped in a well.

metas.name: 14. Lisa the Greek
metas.description: Lisa's ability to pick winning football teams kicks off a strong bond with Homer.

metas.name: 15. Homer Alone
metas.description: A stressed Marge vacations alone, leaving Bart and Lisa with Patty and Selma, and Maggie with Homer--until she leaves in search of Marge.

metas.name: 16. Bart the Lover
metas.description: Bart's answer to detention from Mrs. Krabappel is to answer her personal ad with letters from a Mr. Wonderful, but his last laugh is more of a guilty whimper.

metas.name: 17. Homer at the Bat
metas.description: Burns hires Major League ringers for the plant softball championship.

metas.name: 18. Separate Vocations
metas.description: The results from their aptitude tests cause Bart and Lisa to make 180-degree turns in their behavior.

metas.name: 19. Dog of Death
metas.description: Santa's Little Helper notices resentment after the Simpsons make sacrifices to fund his life-saving operation.

metas.name: 20. Colonel Homer
metas.description: Marge fears a cheatin' heart when a waitress-country singer asks Homer to be her manager.

metas.name: 21. Black Widower
metas.description: Bart suspects something rotten when Selma gets engaged to Sideshow Bob.

metas.name: 22. The Otto Show
metas.description: Spinal Tap hits Springfield, and Otto the bus driver hits the skids after being fired, taking refuge in the Simpsons' garage.

metas.name: 23. Bart's Friend Falls in Love
metas.description: Bart resents Milhouse's new girlfriend; Homer gets the wrong subliminal tape, which has him gaining vocabulary, not losing weight.

metas.name: 24. Brother, Can You Spare Two Dimes?
metas.description: Homer's half-brother asks for a loan after Homer is awarded some cash.
